floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 10 reconfirmed (build 107 vs target 108); mapped 2 coupled gaps (A=folded else recompute, B=tail base-copy) and PROVED Gap A's insn is pure-C-reachable via arm-split (107->108), residual

Structural session: both gaps nailed at RTL (Gap A = cse deletion of the else recompute; Gap B = local_alloc live-range split of the join-block base). Clean structural levers (param types, A+B couplin

frontier.hypothesis: Gap A: break cse's extended-BB propagation into the else block so the a0+3 available-expression does not reach insn 74 (then the recompute survives AND, being live-in from pre-if, is anti-dep-anchored last by sched).
frontier.mechanism: cse extends the pre-if equivalence into the else because the else is a single-predecessor branch target. A control-flow structural change that gives the else block a second predecessor (or otherwise breaks cse_basic_block's path continuation) would stop the fold without touching semantics.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/cse.c cse_basic_block path/next-branch logic; try structural refactors of the if/else that alter the else block's predecessor set (e.g. hoisting a shared post-call statement to create a merge) and measure whether insn 74 survives; if it survives, verify sched anchors it last (target 108, score down from 10).

frontier.hypothesis: Gap B: the tail base copy requires a local_alloc live-range split at the join; raise register pressure across .L800459DC (legitimately) so s1's tail use gets a block-local caller-save copy.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc assigns block-local pseudos (used only in the no-call tail block) to caller-save regs (v0/v1); it currently keeps s1 (global, callee-save) as the direct base. More live values at the join, or a genuinely block-local base pseudo cse cannot fold, would trigger the split copy.
frontier.next_probe: Inspect dump.i.greg/lreg for s1 (reg 77) allocation vs a hypothetical block-local; try directed permuter (PERM_ macros) over tail-store orderings / base-pointer spellings with the clean single-function target.o; measure the tail against `addu v0,s1,zero`.

frontier.hypothesis: Directed permuter on the whole function (fresh-seed) can find a pure-C form that closes one or both RA/scheduling artifacts that hand-derivation has not.
frontier.mechanism: both residuals are RA/scheduling ties; the permuter's structural mutations explore orderings/spellings outside the hand-search space (difficult-is-not-impossible mandates it before any pessimistic claim).
frontier.next_probe: Build a clean single-function target.o (asm/funcs/func_80045878.s + prelude, no .set gp=64), run permuter_campaign.py with --stop-on-zero and fresh-seed discipline; harvest + stop in-turn; vet any closing form against the cheat catalog before proposing.
